survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata for Hong Kong, China, and constructs a student-level binary outcome (digital technology use during sports participation) from two ICT familiarity items. The analytic sample is restricted to Hong Kong because other participating regions (B-S-J-Z, Taipei, Macao) had substantial missingness in ICT/well-being/parent questionnaires, and the authors further removed cases with missing outcome variables and cases with >20% missing independent variables. The manuscript does not report applying PISA sampling weights or replicate weights in the ML training/evaluation; therefore, it is unclear whether complex survey design effects were accounted for in the predictive models. Because the models are trained with Stata/Python and evaluated on a held-out test set, analysts should verify whether any PISA weight variables were used; if not, results may be sensitive to the clustered sampling design and nonresponse patterns.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Data come from PISA 2018 conducted in Hong Kong, China (ICT digital sport module). The authors removed 549 samples with missing outcome variables, and removed 26 samples with >20% missing independent variables (reported as n=563 removed in total for this step). Missing values for continuous predictors were imputed with the median and missing values for categorical predictors were imputed with the plurality. The final analytic sample contained 4925 valid cases. A fixed random seed (175) was set for reproducibility, and the dataset was split into training (85%, n=4186) and test (15%, n=739) sets.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Hong Kong (China) — ICT familiarity items for sports digital participation (student-level)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Test set (AUC/Accuracy/Precision/Recall/F1): GNB AUC=0.700; GBDT AUC=0.641; KNN AUC=0.707; LR AUC=0.717 (best among primary models); Stacking AUC=0.723 with F1=0.166 (reported).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Hong Kong (China) the study leveraged academic performance, weekly number of PE days, household ICT resources, school ICT resources, and ICT social perception to predict Digital Sports participation, finding that household ICT resources and ICT social perception were significant positive correlates while academic performance showed a significant negative association (e.g., AOR for ICT home=1.08; AOR for ICT social perception=1.18; AOR for academic performance=0.995). This indicates that strengthening ICT access at home and improving students’ ICT social environment—alongside maintaining sufficient PE opportunities—may increase uptake of digital sports participation, though the study is correlational and does not report survey-weighted estimation.

data.outcome_summary: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata from Hong Kong, China (n=6,037 initially; final analytic sample n=4,925 after removing 549 cases with missing outcome variables and excluding cases with >20% missing independent variables). The dependent variable is a binary indicator of Digital Sports participation constructed from two ICT familiarity items (time using digital devices for sports inside/outside class). After univariate screening and multilevel logistic regression, five predictors were used to train ML classifiers (Gaussian Naive Bayes, GBDT, KNN, and Logistic Regression) with hyperparameter tuning via GridSearchCV (5-fold CV) and evaluation on a held-out test set. On the test set, AUC ranged from 0.641 to 0.717 for primary models, with Logistic Regression best (AUC=0.717) and a stacking ensemble reaching AUC=0.723. SHAP was used for interpretability, but SHAP feature importance is not causal, and the manuscript does not report applying PISA sampling/replicate weights in the ML pipeline.
